title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and fake social media profiles were used to replicate the likeness of a named, real attorney in order to sell counterfeit legal services to immigrants. The failure did not originate inside any legitimate AI deployment. Instead, actors outside the attorney's control used AI tools to fabricate convincing materials, then distributed them at scale across multiple social media platforms. The platforms served as the distribution layer, and the volume of fake profiles, nearly 6,500 removed by a private anti-piracy firm, indicates the content passed through whatever automated moderation those platforms apply without being flagged or removed until active effort was made to report it.

The specific failure mode is impersonation: a real person's face and professional identity were cloned to generate false authority and trust. The scam then moved off-platform to WhatsApp and email, where fabricated contracts and fraudulent testimonials reinforced the deception. The point at which earlier detection was most plausible was at the platforms themselves, where coordinated inauthentic behavior and repeated use of a single person's likeness across hundreds of accounts could in principle have triggered review. Whether any platform's policies were violated and what those platforms knew is not established by the reporting.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or operating the scheme, whether any authority has identified suspects, and whether any investigation has produced findings.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal's likeness, offering fraudulent immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 cash payments. The scams escalated dramatically in recent months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram.

The scheme typically begins with social media videos directing viewers to contact a WhatsApp number, where scammers exchange emails and send phony contracts. Fraudulent testimonials falsely claim Leal helped clients obtain legal status or secure release from immigration detention. Leal warns consumers to be cautious of requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, noting his office never requests payments over the phone. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scam's origin and urges immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online.
